name: Requirements Management Plan
purpose: The requirements management plan is part of the project management plan and specifies how requirements activities are conducted throughout the project. The planning activities are collecting, analyzing, categorizing, prioritizing, documenting, determining metrics and defining the traceability structure; the managing activities are tracking, reporting, tracing, validating and configuration management. It is developed once and does not usually change.

elements.guidance: Describe how requirements will be collected or elicited, considering techniques such as brainstorming, interviewing and observation.
Describe how requirements will be analyzed for prioritization, categorization and impact on the product or project approach.
Identify the categories for requirements, such as business, stakeholder or quality.
Define how requirements are documented; the format can range from a simple spreadsheet to more elaborate forms with detailed descriptions and attachments.

Identify the prioritization approach. Some requirements are non-negotiable, such as regulatory ones or those needed to comply with organization policy or infrastructure; others are nice to have but not necessary for functionality.

Document the metrics requirements are measured against. The book's example: a requirement to support 150 lb may have a design metric of 120 percent (180 lb), and any decision that takes the product below 120 percent needs customer approval.
Identify the information used to link requirements from their origin to the deliverables that satisfy them.
Describe how often, and with what techniques, progress on requirements is tracked.
Describe how reporting on requirements is conducted and how often.
Identify the methods used to validate requirements, such as inspection, audits, demonstration and testing.
Describe the configuration management system that controls requirements, documentation and the change management process, and the authorization levels needed to approve changes.

tailoring: For smaller projects, combine the requirements management plan with the scope management plan.
If the project involves business analysis, incorporate how business analysis and project management requirements activities interact.
The test and evaluation strategy can be documented in this plan; for larger projects a separate testing plan may be better.
If using an agile or adaptive development approach, incorporate how the backlog is used to manage and track requirements.
agile_or_adaptive: If an agile or adaptive development approach is used, incorporate how the backlog manages and tracks requirements (Tailoring Tips, PDF page 44, printed page 33).
